content.text:
While the inset panel is open (the diff view or the New Project form), nothing beneath it can take focus or keyboard input. Mouse input beneath was already blocked, so the gaps were all keyboard and focus:

- **Tab and Shift+Tab** now cycle focus within the panel, wrapping from last to first. Before, Tab could walk out onto the chat input and other elements beneath. This uses gpui-kit's built-in focus trap.
- **Focus moved from beneath:** anything that tries to focus an element beneath, such as a task finishing, has focus sent back to wherever it was last inside the panel. If that isn't known, it goes to the panel's content. The same happens if focus is lost entirely, which used to fall back to the chat input.
- **Blocked shortcuts:** Ctrl+P (the palette) and Ctrl+F1 (collapsing the ribbon) do nothing while the panel is open. Cmd replaces Ctrl on macOS.
- **Still allowed:** Ctrl+, (the settings window), quitting, and Esc to close the panel.

**Tests:** the floating-diff test now opens the diff and checks that:
- focus starts inside the panel and stays there after six Tabs and a Shift+Tab;
- after the chat input is focused from beneath, focus is back in the panel;
- Ctrl+P and Ctrl+F1 leave the palette closed and the ribbon expanded.

I disabled the focus-return handler temporarily and the test failed at that check, then restored it. The test window has to be activated first, because gpui only reports focus leaving an element in an active window. The suite shows 133 passed, 1 skipped (it needs the real harness), and the same palette test failing as before. The build has no warnings.

**Spec:** `InsetPanelScope` has a new `modal` section covering all of the above. `piton check` and `piton build check` pass, and I ran `piton build`.

The code is in `src/inset_panel.rs` and `src/main_window.rs`. I haven't tried it in the running app.
